name: Premco Global Ltd
tagline: Tiny, honest-management narrow-elastic-fabric maker (supplies Page/Jockey, Lux, Dollar, Rupa; India + Vietnam) with a long dividend record — but a decade of flat sales, a loss-making FY26 on US textile tariffs, ~50% India utilisation, a new capex that isn't paying off and CEO churn
business_overview: Manufacturer of elastic and non-elastic woven/knitted narrow fabrics, tapes and webbings used in innerwear and apparel. Supplies most major Indian innerwear brands (Page/Jockey, Lux, Dollar, Rupa) plus exports; a Vietnam subsidiary (lower power cost and ~8.5% tax) serves the US market. New Umargaon (Gujarat) plant (~Rs 18 Cr capex, ~Rs 50 Cr peak sales potential) is ramping; a Palghar plant was closed and sold (FY25), proceeds paid out as a special dividend.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 130 Cr; stock ~-47% from a ~Rs 685 peak (52w low ~Rs 365)
Net sales ~Rs 21.4 Cr (-24% YoY); small net loss; EBITDA collapsed ~97% YoY
Into losses (India operations described by a long-term holder as 'a disaster'); Vietnam also hit by ~20% US duty
Net cash historically; consistent dividends even in weak quarters
Aspires to ~Rs 200 Cr revenue in ~5 years (from ~Rs 100 Cr), ~17-18% operating margin; new CEO after Mr Panwar's resignation (Jul 2025)
fundamentals_narrative: Premco is a decades-old, owner-run microcap with genuinely honest management and an unbroken dividend habit, but the business has barely grown in ten years (~Rs 66 Cr sales in 2014, ~Rs 70 Cr in 2023) despite adding Vietnam and now Umargaon capacity. FY26 tipped into losses: a 50% US tariff on Indian textiles hit direct and indirect exports, Vietnam took a ~20% US duty, and crude-linked polyester/nylon/rubber costs rose faster than the company could pass through. India utilisation is ~50%, the new capex is not yet contributing, the long-serving CEO resigned, and the Rs 200 Cr-in-5-years aspiration implies a growth rate the company has never delivered. Even its largest long-term holder (an elevated user) has turned critical on capital allocation and 'lack of hunger for growth'.
sentiment_summary: Small, long-running thread dominated by two long-term holders — HIMSHAH (holder since 2005, stresses management honesty) and dd1474 (top-10 holding, detailed AGM notes) — plus a persistent bear (Aarti: fragmented, low-margin industry, capex without sales, PE too high). dd1474 has moved from patient bull to openly critical: 'very poor management of affairs', 'not expecting any magical swing'.
community_signal: No trusted 'buy' call. The most engaged elevated user (dd1474) is now critical of execution and capital allocation. Discovery candidate, theme-rank 2 (no live-theme keyword match; textile-adjacent but no keyword hit).
key_new_facts: FY26 turned loss-making; Q4 FY26 sales -24% YoY, EBITDA down ~97%.
50% US tariff on Indian textiles hit direct + indirect exports; Vietnam hit by ~20% US duty.
India utilisation ~50%; new Umargaon plant not yet contributing; Palghar plant closed & sold, proceeds paid as special dividend.
Long-serving CEO (Mr Panwar) resigned Jul 2025; new CEO to be assessed.
Management aspires to ~Rs 200 Cr revenue in ~5 years at ~17-18% margin — a pace never previously achieved.
bull_case: Honest, owner-run management; unbroken dividend record even through weak quarters
Very small equity/float — modest sales/margin recovery would lever EPS
Supplies all major Indian innerwear brands; Vietnam gives a low-cost export base
bear_case: ~Decade of flat sales despite capacity additions; new capex not paying off
FY26 losses on US textile tariffs (India + Vietnam) and crude-linked input inflation
Fragmented, low-margin industry (~80% unorganised); top-5 customers ~60% of revenue
CEO churn; largest long-term holder now critical of execution
verdict_headline: Honest but chronically no-growth narrow-fabric microcap, loss-making in FY26 on US tariffs, with capex that isn't working — 'neither', Low conviction
verdict_reasoning: Discovery candidate, theme-rank 2 (no live-theme keyword match — recency discovery).

four_box score 1.0 (tailwind no — US textile-tariff headwind on India + Vietnam, structural competition from unorganised players; tam weak — ~Rs 130 Cr mcap but a decade of ~Rs 100 Cr flat sales and a 5-year aspiration it has never matched; moat no — fragmented low-margin narrow-fabric commodity, customer concentration; valuation weak — P/E elevated vs an ~11x historical average, on depressed/loss earnings). Score <= 1.5 -> thesis_fit 'neither', hard.

The US tariff is a recent negative catalyst, but it compounds an already-broken domestic operation and a decade of stagnation in a fragmented commodity business — treated as impairing / normal treatment, not a non-impairing speed-breaker.
No red_flag_tier (owner-run, honest, dividend-paying; a loss year is not a going concern).

Conviction Low: management integrity and a dividend habit are the only positives; growth is absent, FY26 is loss-making, the new capex isn't contributing, and the most engaged elevated holder has turned critical. First-time read.
